For each $n\geq1$, select a finite $1/n$-net $F_n\subseteq X$, and define
\[
D=\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}F_n.
\]
Each $F_n$ is finite, so $D$ is countable. If $x\in X$ and $U$ is an open neighborhood of $x$, choose $r>0$ with $B_r(x)\subseteq U$, and then choose $n$ with $1/n<r$. Since $F_n$ is a $1/n$-net, there is $y\in F_n$ with $d(x,y)<1/n<r$, so $y\in U\cap D$. Thus $D$ is dense in $X$. Therefore $X$ is separable.
\end{proof}
